outcome: blood glucose levels (fasting, after breakfast, after lunch, after dinner)
cohort: The study included 180 pregnant women with hyperglycemia, randomized to receive either quercetin or melatonin treatment from the 15th to the 33rd week of pregnancy.
finding: Melatonin treatment resulted in a lower rate of primary composite neonatal outcomes (20%) and significantly improved glycemic control compared to quercetin treatment (34.12% for primary composite neonatal outcomes).
mod_finding: Labor pains were induced in more women in the quercetin group (58.54%) compared to the melatonin group (50.29%), but this difference was not statistically significant.
followup_time: At birth/shortly after birth for neonatal outcomes; during pregnancy for maternal outcomes and glycemic control.
birth_weight: Melatonin group: 3211 ± 82.4 g; Quercetin group: 3232 ± 100.28 g.
